subject: Mini-session vs continuous-context billing — clarification requested

Cc: procure@acmeretail.com

Subject: Clarify billing behavior for short interactive sessions vs long continuous context

Hi Logan,

Quick question from our procurement and ML infra teams as we prepare for a Dedicated pilot: we run two main interaction patterns and want to make sure billing aligns with our cost model. Can you confirm how Redwood treats these scenarios for billing and rounding/minimums?

1) Short interactive "mini-sessions": lots of 6–12 turn conversations (user prompt + 1–2 assistant turns) repeatedly across many users. Typical tokens per call ~120–800.
2) Long continuous context: single conversation threads where we append documents and history over days (20k–60k tokens retained in the context; model sometimes truncated via prefixing).

Specific asks:
- Does Redwood aggregate short calls into a conversation window for amortization (i.e., avoid charging full min-charge every call)? If so, what is the default window and how is it defined?
- When switching models mid-conversation (e.g., from a smaller Llama-2 variant to a higher-capacity model for a heavy query), is the context treated as one billing session or does that trigger a new billing window?
- How does rounding work for streaming responses vs. non-streamed generation? Is there a minimum quantum and is it the same across model classes?
- Any guidance on discounting mechanics if we commit to a dedicated pool but have mixed mini-session and continuous-context traffic?

I've attached a small CSV sample of our traffic by hour to illustrate patterns. Happy to do a short call if it's easier.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Head of ML Ops — Acme Retail
procure@acmeretail.com

Hi Sarah — thanks, good questions. Below is a practical breakdown with numbers that should map to your CSV. I kept it non-legal and focused on how usage would be measured and rounded under our standard Dedicated rules (we can adjust for pilot contracts).

Summary of key rules (current default):
- Conversation window: 30-minute amortization window by conversation_id. Any calls that re-use the same conversation_id within 30 minutes are treated as the same session for the purposes of minimums/quantum amortization.
- Quantum (rounding): we round up to the nearest 100-token quantum for non-streamed completions on the small/medium models and to 250 tokens for large/extended-context families by default. Streaming responses round to the nearest 50-token quantum per finalized chunk, with a 30-token streaming minimum per response.
- Model switch: switching model family mid-conversation closes the previous session for billing (new model -> new session) unless you explicitly set model_variants to be billed as compatible in the rollout config. That means context tokens re-ingested under the new model count toward a new session.
- KV/prefix reuse credit: if the runtime can reuse KV cache without re-encoding the full context (same conversation_id, same model family), we apply a partial credit equal to the cost of the reused tokens (this appears as a negative line-item in usage exports).
- Minimums: there is a per-session floor of 150 tokens for mini-session traffic if a session is marked as 'interactive' (low-latency) — this is to prevent micro-call abuse. The 150-token floor is amortized inside the 30-minute window.

Example scenarios (numbers approximate):
A) Mini-session pattern — 6 turns, average tokens per turn: user 80, assistant 160 => ~240 tokens per call.
- Quantum: round up to nearest 100 -> 300 tokens billed per call.
- If same conversation_id and calls happen every 10 minutes during an hour, first call bills 300 tokens (subject to 150 floor), subsequent calls within 30 minutes are billed with incremental tokens and benefit from prefix reuse where applicable. Over the hour you'd see less than naive sum because of amortization.

B) Continuous long-context (e.g., 40k tokens retained).
- We bill the tokens actually processed by the model each call. For long contexts we encourage using our context-slicing APIs so you only re-send deltas; otherwise re-encoding a 40k prefix is expensive and will be billed as such.
- Rounding quantum for large/extended families: 250-token buckets. So a 3,120-token generation rounds to 3,250 tokens.

C) Model switch mid-conversation:
- If you move from a medium family (100-token quantum) to an extended family (250-token quantum) for a heavy query, the runtime treats the switch as starting a new session. Any KV cache tied to the previous family is not reused unless you use our cross-compat opt-in which incurs a conversion cost. Practically: expect a one-time higher charge when you switch for the initial warm-up.

Attachments attached: I exported a short workbook with worked examples based on your CSV buckets (model_switch_examples.xlsx) and a quick one-pager on quanta (redwood_billing_quanta.pdf).

If you want, we can run your CSV through a quick script and return an estimated monthly invoice under different packaging options. Monica — please advise on packaging options (committed pool sizing, tiered discounts) we should show.

— Karthik

Hi Sarah — I pulled together a few commercial options that map to the traffic patterns Karthik outlined. High level: if you commit to a monthly Dedicated pool we can: 

- Offer an "interactive bundle": a tier that optimizes for mini-session workloads — lower quantum for common mid-size models (100-token quantum -> 50-token effective billing via smoothing) and a 10% committed discount on top of list.
- Offer an "extended-context pack": credits for long-context warm-up and a longer amortization window for prefix reuse (we can extend to 90 minutes for a contractual commitment to a minimum committed context-month).
- Include a one-time warm-up credit to offset the model-switch cost in quarter 1 of the pilot (applies to the first model transition event).

If you'd like, we can produce two sample invoices for April under (A) pure pay-as-you-go, (B) 12-month committed pool with the interactive bundle + 10% discount. Karthik — please flag any technical caveats about extending amortization windows beyond the default.

Sarah — would you be open to a 30-minute call Thursday to walk the CSV with us and agree which packaging to model? I'll bring a simple invoice simulator and contract-appropriate language for the warm-up credit and quantum smoothing.
